papers.title: Integrating niches of the pathogen, multiple host and vector species highlights abiotic constraints and host‐vector interactions shaping pine wilt disease risk in China
papers.authors: Wang Wen-quan, Ting Du, Jiangxia Ye, Xiaohong Huang, Yangyang Li
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pine wilt disease (PWD), caused by Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (PWN), is a major threat to forest health and pest management in China. Because PWD results from interactions among the pathogen, vector insects, and host plants, single-component analyses may misrepresent disease risk and overlook species-specific contributions. We integrated the environmental niches of the pathogen, hosts, and vectors to characterize abiotic constraints and biotic influences on PWD risk, quantify species-specific contributions and interactions, and inform surveillance priorities. RESULTS: Ensemble ecological niche models were developed for PWN, 17 susceptible hosts, and 10 potential cerambycid vectors across China and integrated with GeoDetector analysis. Although suitability patterns were broadly consistent, PWN had a much narrower suitable range than hosts and vectors, and this concordance declined under future climate scenarios. Bioclimatic variables were the primary determinants of habitat suitability for most species, whereas PWN showed narrower optimal ranges for key environmental drivers than most hosts and vectors. papers.title: A model for the spatial population dynamics of the European invasion of the Japanese beetle (Popillia japonica)
papers.authors: Davide Martinetti, Laura Erbetta, Danièle Bevacqua, Olivier Bonnefon, Marino Gatto
papers.abstract: Popillia japonica is an invasive beetle first detected in Northern Italy in 2014 and considered as one of the most dangerous pests for crops due to the economic, environmental, and social costs by European phytosanitary authorities. Here we develop a process-based model for quantifying the invasion dynamics of P. japonica with the goal to elaborate risk maps for the design of surveillance and control strategies. The proposed spatially heterogeneous model captures the different behaviors of both adults, which drive the invasion through flight and short-distance human-mediated transport, and ovo-larval stages, which affect demography due to their susceptibility to environmental conditions. Both processes are biologically informed through variables that are known to influence population dynamics, namely the number of summer days, affecting the flight ability of the adults, and the environmental suitability for larval survival. The simulated presence of adult beetles is then contrasted to pest observation data at the municipality scale from Northern Italy and Switzerland from the initial invasion to December 2023. papers.title: Citizen Science and Environmental DNA Reveals Site of an Invasive Paropsisterna beata (Newman) (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) Population in New Zealand
papers.authors: Toni M. Withers, Andrew R. Pugh, Darryl A. Herron, Dean Satchell, Shaun Wilkinson
papers.source: OpenAlex / New Zealand Journal of Zoology
papers.abstract: More than a decade after being declared eradicated, a population of the Australian blessed leaf beetle Paropsisterna beata (Coleoptera: Chrysomelidae) was located in New Zealand in 2026. The pest has been found and photographed three times by citizen scientists approximately 25 km north of the original Wellington infestation and reported on iNaturalist. An environmental DNA (eDNA) match from a water sample then directed searching to Eucalyptus trees visible on Google Earth upstream. This sequence of events leading to finding an established population highlights the potential for citizen science observations and eDNA monitoring to both uncover and pinpoint a cryptic pest's location as part of biosecurity surveillance.

papers.title: Current applications of artificial intelligence for advancing agriculture, sustainability and climate mitigation
papers.authors: Mostafa Farajpour
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping agriculture by enabling data-driven decision-making across crop production systems and supporting the transition toward more sustainable, resilient, and climate-smart farming. This review critically synthesizes advances in AI applications spanning precision irrigation, nutrient and soil management, yield prediction, pest and disease monitoring, computer vision, autonomous agricultural robotics, and large language model (LLM)-based decision support systems. Beyond summarizing technological developments, the review evaluates their practical deployment, emphasizing that successful agricultural AI depends not only on predictive accuracy but also on model generalizability, explainability, economic feasibility, interoperability, and integration with existing agronomic knowledge. Emerging technologies including Vision Transformers, foundation models, Digital Twins, multimodal AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, and federated and continual learning—are discussed as important directions for overcoming limitations related to data scarcity, environmental variability, and scalable field implementation. papers.abstract: The Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) remains one of the most destructive pests affecting cotton productivity, with infestation levels strongly driven by climatic fluctuations and crop phenology.This study presents a machine learning-based framework for early multi-classification and prediction of Pink Bollworm incidence using agro-meteorological variables.The dataset includes maximum and minimum air temperature, relative humidity, rainfall, sunshine hours, evaporation, and wind speed, all of which influence Pink Bollworm development, migration, and reproductive cycles.After preprocessing, applying cyclic encoding to temporal variables, and generating lagged climatic features, multiple machine learning algorithms-including SVM, Neural Networks, KNN, Regression models, Ensemble methods, and Naïve Bayes-were trained and systematically compared.SVM model demonstrated the best test accuracy, effectively capturing dynamic climate-pest interactions.The resulting MATLAB-based classification tool enables rapid assessment and supports climate-informed pest surveillance.A stratified 80:20 train-test split was employed, with 5-fold cross-validation on the training set for hyperparamete

papers.title: Sensitivity evaluation and multi-omics analysis of Bursaphelenchus xylophilus populations to emamectin benzoate in Shandong province field
papers.authors: Kunyang Ju, Zhifan Ma, Shuhan Guo, YuKe Wang, Shengnan Dong
papers.abstract: Pine trees provide substantial ecological and economic benefits worldwide, including water conservation, timber production, and carbon sequestration. However, Bursaphelenchus xylophilus , as the pathogen of pine wilt disease (PWD), results in extensive pine mortality annually, posing a serious threat to global pine resources and environmental security. Currently, chemical control remains the primary strategy for managing PWD. In Shandong Province, emamectin benzoate (EB) is the main nematicide for trunk injection. Nevertheless, long-term use of a single compound carries a high risk of resistance development. In this study, the sensitivity of 15 B. xylophilus strains from different regions of Shandong Province to EB was evaluated. The highest and lowest LC 50 values were observed in the PL (320.99 μg•mL -1 ) and CD strains (114.63 μg•mL -1 ), respectively, yielding a resistance ratio (PL vs CD) of 2.8 < 5, indicating that EB resistance may not have developed in the B. xylophilus populations in Shandong. papers.title: Colonial Alien: House Crows, Disposability and Necropolitics in Urban Tanzania
papers.authors: Paul Chacha Mahere, Samwel Moses Ntapanta, Samuel Kettler
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Which lives are allowed to flourish in the city, and which are rendered excessive, alien, or disposable? This article examines kunguru (a Swahili term for crows/ravens, commonly referring to the house crow, Corvus splendens , in urban Tanzania) in Dar es Salaam as a lens through which to analyze colonial afterlives, urban waste infrastructures, and the biopolitics of multispecies life in a postcolonial African city. Kunguru in urban East Africa were initially introduced to Zanzibar Island by the British colonial administration as scavengers and were incorporated into urban hygiene projects. Over time, however, their ecological success exceeded the narrow functions assigned to them, leading to their reclassification as invasive aliens and subsequent targets of eradication. Kunguru introduced in Tanzania through colonial ecological interventions are presently proliferating by fragmented waste infrastructures and governed as unwanted excess in the contemporary postcolonial cities of Tanzania. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: Despite the significant contribution of HAIs to increased morbidity, mortality, length of hospital stay, and escalating health care costs, they continue to be a major public health problem globally.New and fast spreading "MDROs" (Multidrug Resistant Pathogens) including MRSA (Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus), VRE (Vancomycin-resistant Enterococci), ESBL (Extended-spectrum β-lactamase) producing Enterobacteriaceae, CRE (carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae), Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa have further contributed to the complexity of infection management in hospital settings.Due to the various resistance mechanisms such as enzymatic degradation, induction of efflux pumps, alteration of permeability and biofilm formation, there are limited therapeutic options and poor clinical outcomes available for these pathogens.This systematic review will assess the effectiveness of complete hospital infection control with an emphasis on infection prevention and control (IPC) interventions, surveillance tools and antimicrobial stewardship programs (ASPs).The standard and transmission based precautions, environmental hygiene and device associated IPC bundles (CLA

papers.title: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) cultivation in India: A critical review of status, constraints and future directions
papers.authors: A Dharshni, C. P. Ravindran, S. Muthulakshmi, S. Shenbagavalli, T Anitha
papers.abstract: Strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa Duch.) is an economically important berry crop worldwide, due to its distinctive flavour, nutritional value and health benefits. In recent years, it has been cultivated not only in temperate regions, but also in subtropical and tropical regions. It has become one of the high-value horticultural crops in India, due to the growing consumer demand and good returns to farmers. This review critically examines the trends in yield, constraints and technological factors influencing strawberry cultivation across major strawberry producing states such as Maharashtra, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and other emerging regions in India. Evidence from existing studies indicates that the adoption of improved cultivation practices such as balanced fertilisation, integrated pest management, mulching, protected cultivation and soilless systems has substantially improved fruit yield and quality compared to conventional open-field methods. papers.abstract: Fall armyworm (FAW) is a major constraint in maize production and cause considerable yield loss. Although chemical control methods are being widely used for management of FAW, there are increasing concerns regarding issues like pesticide resistance and ecological imbalance. Exploiting host plant resistance represents the most eco-friendly and cost-effective approach. Growing resistant varieties are one of the ecofriendly approach in FAW management. A prime phase in the line of research is identification of resistant sources and underlying mechanisms contributing towards resistance. Present study integrates field screening, ovipositional preference assay, volatile profiling, and olfactory behavioural assays to characterize resistance in maize genotypes against FAW. Initial screening trials across two seasons revealed a dominance of susceptible genotypes, with DMRE 63 exhibiting resistance and CML 122 as moderate resistance. Leaf damage was highest at 14 days after infestation which corresponds to late larval feeding stage. papers.title: Digital twin forestry as an informatics framework integrating remote sensing ecosystem modelling and data assimilation
papers.authors: Niamjit Das, Kevin Andrew
papers.abstract: Forests are essential to the Earth system, regulating carbon, water, and biodiversity cycles while underpinning ecosystem resilience. Yet they face mounting pressures from climate and land-use change, requiring integrative informatics approaches that link high-resolution observations with advanced ecosystem models. This systematic review defines Digital Twin Forestry (DTF) as an emerging paradigm that continuously couples multisensor Earth Observation data with ecosystem models through data assimilation, enabling dynamic, uncertainty-aware forecasting and adaptive decision support. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we synthesized 57 peer-reviewed studies published between 2016 and 2025 that combined EO datasets with ecosystem modeling and assimilation frameworks. Demonstrated advances include CubeSat constellations, spaceborne LiDAR, UAV hyperspectral systems, and hybrid machine-learning surrogates. Data assimilation methods such as Ensemble Kalman Filters and Particle Filters serve as computational bridges between multi-temporal observations and dynamic model states. papers.abstract: The bark beetle Dendroctonus micans (Kug.) (Coleoptera, Curculionidae, Scolytinae), a pest of spruce and pine, probably originates from eastern Siberia. Its closest relative is the North American D. punctatus (LeConte), on the other side of the Behring Strait. D. micans has largely spread westward and is presently established in most of the spruce forests of Eurasia. In newly colonised territories, it is considered as a tree-killing pest. A very specific predator, Rhizophagus grandis (Coleoptera, Monotomidae), has followed its prey in its territorial expansion, with temporal and spatial lags due to long distance passive transportation of D. micans with trade, and to habitat fragmentation. When both species coexist, D. micans is very sparce and only occasionally kills trees, because the high capacity of R. grandis to locate prey even at very low densities enables it to control the pest. This very particular relationship has been exploited for biological control. Mass production and inoculative releases of R. grandis have been undertaken in four countries: Georgia since 1963, France (1978), Great Britain (1983) and Türkiye (1985). Objective. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Hypoxia is closely associated with tumor progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and diagnostic challenges. The timely detection of hypoxia in live cancer cells is critical for early cancer diagnosis and for monitoring the effectiveness of anticancer therapies. Recently, there has been growing interest in non-covalent supramolecular design strategies for the development of hypoxia-sensitive sensors and prodrugs. Unlike the widely employed covalent approach, supramolecular chemistry eliminates the need for complex and time-consuming synthetic processes. Instead, the individual components of the sensor autonomously self-assemble into the desired structure. This review provides an overview of hypoxia-targeted and hypoxia-activated supramolecular probes, along with their mechanisms of action in tumor diagnosis and therapy. The supramolecular systems considered are classified according to the use of certain classes of macrocycles. The role of macrocyclic derivatives in the various proposed approaches and the response patterns of hypoxic targets will also be analyzed. Their implementation of important parts like Raspberry Pi 4 as an AI inference module and an STM32 microcontroller as an actuator controller accelerates the responsiveness, increases security, and saves energy consumption since there is no need in cloud computing. Using the local climatic and soil moisture data the machine learning model identifies optimum irrigation time and duration looking at various parameters such as temperature, humidity, rain and crop-specific thresholds. The whole decision-making process is automated and carried out at the edge that makes it functional even without interruption in areas with poor or no internet connection. papers.title: Similar degenerative patterns of olfactory receptor genes in the giant panda and marine carnivores
papers.authors: LiWen Kang, Junjie Chen, Mingsheng Hong, Wei Wei, Zuofu Xiang
papers.abstract: Olfactory receptor (OR) genes constitute the largest mammalian gene family and are critical for olfactory perception and ecological adaptation. OR gene variation is associated with interspecific differences in habitat, diet, and sensory reliance, yet the relative contributions of these ecological factors to OR evolution remain unclear. Here, we systematically analyzed OR repertoires across 25 carnivoran species occupying diverse niches. Marine carnivorans exhibit convergent OR degeneration, with fewer intact genes and ancestral orthologs, higher pseudogene ratios, and relaxed purifying selection compared with terrestrial species. Notably, bamboo-specialized giant pandas display identical degenerative signatures, possessing the smallest intact OR repertoire and most lost ancestral OR groups among terrestrial carnivorans. Our models show habitat primarily shapes intact OR quantity, while dietary specialization governs pseudogenization and selective constraints. These findings reveal convergent OR functional decay under aquatic adaptation and extreme dietary specialization, illustrating complex links between lifestyle and chemosensory genome evolution in mammals.

papers.authors: Bashir Olaniyi Sadiq, Mohammed Dahiru Buhari, IBRAHIM ADABARA, Enerst Edozie, Asaba Shabiluh
papers.abstract: The rapid digitization of modern systems has increased the demand for intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven solutions across connected systems. Although deep convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have substantially advanced classification accuracy over the last decade, standard architectures such as VGG, ResNet, and plain CNNs often struggle to jointly optimize accuracy, parameter efficiency, and robustness to intra-class variation. papers.abstract: The widespread proliferation of electromagnetic technologies in communications, healthcare, and daily life poses increasing risks of radiation-induced tissue injury. Mitigating these deleterious effects remains a formidable challenge. Recently, medical gases, including molecular hydrogen (H2), hydrogen sulfide (H2S), carbon monoxide (CO), nitric oxide (NO), and hyperbaric oxygen, have emerged as a promising therapeutic modality with radioprotective potential. These gases exert their effects through integrated, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and mitochondrial-protective mechanisms. Specifically, the endogenous gasotransmitters (CO, NO, and H2S) modulate precise signaling networks, while the exogenous interventions (H2, and hyperbaric oxygen) function primarily through direct radical scavenging or the induction of hormetic stress responses. This review evaluates the research progress of these five medical gases in preventing and treating injuries across the electromagnetic spectrum. papers.abstract: As successive rounds of multilateral negotiation pushed average industrial tariffs down from the double digits of the immediate post-war years to low single figures, the frictions that decide who trades and who does not have quietly migrated. They have moved off the customs schedule and into the rule book. This paper follows that migration and asks what it has meant for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). papers.abstract: Postharvest diseases remain among the most critical factors limiting the shelf life, quality, and marketability of fresh produce worldwide, contributing substantially to economic losses and food insecurity. Although conventional preservation strategies such as synthetic fungicides and low-temperature storage have been effective, their long-term use is increasingly constrained by pathogen resistance, chemical residue concerns, environmental impacts, and stricter regulatory controls. In recent years, probiotic microorganisms and biological control agents (BCAs), particularly when incorporated into edible coating systems, have emerged as promising and bio-based approaches for postharvest disease management. These bio-based systems provide multifunctional benefits by integrating direct antimicrobial activity with competitive exclusion of pathogens, induction of host defense responses, and modulation of fruit physiological processes, while simultaneously forming protective barriers that regulate gas exchange and moisture loss. RNA interference offers sequence-guided suppression of nematode gene expression without requiring a conventional toxicant to act on a broad physiological target. papers.abstract: Abstract Saproxylic beetles are a highly diverse group of tree‐associated insects that play key roles in forest ecosystem functioning, comprising both rare primeval relicts and taxa of economic importance in timber production. Morphological identification of these beetles remains challenging due to high similarity among species‐rich taxa and a number of taxonomic specialists. While European DNA barcode reference databases have expanded in recent years, they remain dominated by western and northern populations, leaving Central and Eastern European taxa heavily underrepresented. Because previous studies have revealed pronounced east–west genetic divergence in several saproxylic beetle species, expanding barcode coverage in Central and Eastern Europe is highly necessary. papers.title: Before Qualia, Strategic Existence Begins
papers.authors: Angelina Inesia-Forde
papers.abstract: Before evolution can select anything, a physically possible causal architecture must already exist for selection to exploit. The T4 bacteriophage, a mindless nanoscale machine whose structure executes functions that map onto both empowering and disempowering strategies in Forde's framework of social dynamics, demonstrates this principle at the nanoscale. The strategies mapped include security, knowledge, hope, fairness, unity, and dignity, alongside their darker counterparts: nativism, hierarchy, misinformation, subjugation, dehumanization, and fear. Each concept is paired with a specific biological mechanism, virion stability, irreversible adsorption, superinfection exclusion, among others, showing that the mapping is grounded in observable structure. These mappings do not reify nonhuman organisms or attribute human qualities to mindless machines. They are structural descriptions: the concepts name functions that the architecture performs, not feelings that the organism experiences. papers.title: Recent plant photosynthate as a driver of ecological and evolutionary processes
papers.authors: David Johnson, Hannah M. Griffiths
papers.abstract: Summary Plants rapidly allocate carbon from photosynthesis belowground via root exudates and root‐associated microorganisms. Here we synthesise recent evidence of our understanding of the consequences of this ‘fast’ pathway of recent photosynthate flux for major ecological and evolutionary processes. This rapid input of plant‐derived carbon to soils shapes food webs and drives processes including soil CO 2 efflux, nutrient cycling, plant community dynamics, stability of symbioses and evolution of contrasting modes of nutrition, such as parasitism and mycoheterotrophy. We also highlight how seasonality and anthropogenic and natural perturbations likely determine the magnitude and dynamics of this fast pathway across major vegetation types, but these factors remain understudied. Further gaps in understanding include demonstrating causal links between photosynthate flow and key biogeochemical cycling processes and the capture of photosynthate by co‐occurring root‐associated microorganisms.

papers.authors: Xu-Ri Xu-Ri, Jiaoneng Yu, Songbo Qu, Tian-Liang, Ribu Shama
papers.abstract: Symbiotic nitrogen fixation (SNF) by legumes is a major natural source of reactive nitrogen that supports ecosystem functioning and carbon sequestration. Warming across the Tibetan Plateau alpine permafrost region may trigger substantial shifts in vegetation composition and distribution, yet the consequences for ecosystem nitrogen inputs remain poorly understood. Here, using 1047 plant samples from 323 plots across the Tibetan Plateau and 15N natural-abundance techniques, we quantify legume and non-legume nitrogen sources and regional aboveground SNF rates. Aboveground SNF is tightly linked to legume aboveground biomass, ranges from 0 to 7.43 g N m−2 yr−1, and peaks at elevations of 3600–4000 m. At the regional scale, its spatial distribution largely coincides with recent decadal gains in aboveground biomass and plant nitrogen density. Process-based simulations show that removing SNF causes severe nitrogen limitation and shifts these ecosystems from a carbon sink to a source. Our findings highlight the important role of legumes in sustaining carbon sinks in Tibetan Plateau permafrost ecosystems. papers.abstract: Moth bean (Vigna aconitifolia (Jacq.) Maréchal) is an underutilised, climate-resilient grain legume well adapted to the arid and semi-arid regions of the Indian subcontinent. Despite its exceptional tolerance to drought and heat, its genetic improvement has been constrained by a narrow-cultivated gene pool, limited genomic resources and the underutilisation of wild relatives. As climate change increases the occurrence of abiotic and biotic stresses, broadening the genetic base of moth beans has become essential for developing resilient and high-yielding cultivars. papers.abstract: Smart polymers undergo reversible physicochemical changes in response to stimuli such as magnetic fields, temperature, pH, light, and external reagents. Advanced polymerization techniques, including reversible addition fragmentation chain transfer (RAFT), atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP), and ring opening polymerization, enable precise control over polymer architecture and functional group placement, allowing the design of tailored responsive materials. These polymers are widely explored in biomedical applications, drug delivery, biosensing, cosmetics, and soft robotics due to their ability to adapt dynamically to environmental conditions. Poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) is a well-known thermoresponsive polymer extensively studied for drug delivery and sensing. Responsive polymers exist in linear, block, graft, and cross-linked forms, with activation depending on interactions between structural motifs and stimuli. Despite promising results, challenges remain, including immunogenicity, batch variability, synthesis complexity, scalability, and limited understanding of in vivo stimulus accessibility. papers.title: Historical dynamics of social adaptation strategies under natural hazard characteristics in the Hengduan Mountains, Southwest China
papers.authors: Xueyuan Huang, Yiping Fang, Xinjun He, Liang Emlyn Yang
papers.source: OpenAlex / Humanities and Social Sciences Communications
papers.abstract: The nexus between natural hazard events and regional societal responses constitutes a critical link in the chain of climate change impacts on human social systems. China’s extensive historical documentary resources remain underutilized for reconstructing spatiotemporal patterns of natural hazard events, characterizing impacts, and identifying adaptation features. This study systematically compiles a dataset of natural hazard events in the Hengduan Mountains region (HMR) during the Little Ice Age (LIA), and delineates their spatiotemporal patterns across climatic fluctuations. An examination of societal adaptation across ten stages reveals the transformation of traditional mountain societies from infrastructure restoration to integrated hazard-relief systems. Results indicate that natural hazard events in the HMR exhibit phased clustering, with one primary peak and four secondary peaks. These clusters are concentrated in land-water ecotones, forming three coupled hazard zones: tectonic-dominated, agroecologically vulnerable, and monsoon-sensitive hydrological zones. papers.title: Global Research Trends in Tick-Borne Diseases of Livestock: A Bibliometric Analysis
papers.abstract: Tick-borne diseases (TBDs) are a critical limitation of livestock health and productivity on the international arena as they result in huge economic losses and emerging challenges due to changing environmental conditions.The objective of the current study was to examine the current trends in the world in terms of the research on tickborne livestock diseases through the use of bibliometric methodology.A structured search strategy was used to retrieve publications indexed in PubMed database between 2020 and 2026 and 2,405 records were included in the analysis.The place of bibliometric analysis was conducted with the help of Bibliometrix (R 4.5.2) and VOSviewer to assess the trends of publications, top contributors, collaboration networks, and theme development.The findings revealed a more or less fluctuating but generally speaking increasing pattern in scientific production with the highest production expected in 2025.China, Brazil and the United States were found to be the most prolific nations with some of the most renowned research institutions like Obihiro University of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine and Universidade Federal de Goiás in the center stage.Through co-authorship

papers.title: Powdery mildew in Eucalyptus spp. clonal mini gardens in Uruguay
papers.authors: Susana Tiscornia, Guillermo Morera, Gonzalo Martínez, Raquel Alonso, Sandra Lupo
papers.abstract: Powdery mildew is a fungal disease that poses a significant threat to global Eucalyptus cultivation; yet the species-level identity of causal agents often remains unresolved due to the limitations of morphological diagnosis. Here, the first estimates of powdery mildew incidence in Eucalyptus clonal mini gardens in Uruguay is provided, and the first approach of species identification within this system is presented. Surveys across three industrial nurseries revealed an overall powdery mildew incidence exceeding 70%, with noteworthy temporal variation and differences among clones. Molecular analyses, using DNA-based identification tools targeting the ITS and LSU rDNA regions, confirmed the presence of Podosphaera pannosa, previously identified in Eucalyptus grandis infections based only on morphological characteristics. Furthermore, this study reports, for the first time, P. aphanis, P. cfr. ruborum and an undescribed Podosphaera species infecting Eucalyptus dunnii in Uruguay. The results highlight the strong influence of host genotype on disease dynamics, with some clones exhibiting consistently lower susceptibility. papers.title: Resource subsidies mediated by non-native species: a review
papers.authors: Letícia Alves, Janeide de Assis Guilherme Padilha, Phillip Joschka Haubrock, Amanda L. Subalusky, Ronaldo Sousa
papers.abstract: Non-native species are recognized as one of the major drivers of biodiversity change globally, with profound impacts on ecosystem functions and services. Despite the high number of studies on non-native species published, mainly in the last two decades, an often-overlooked aspect is their role as mediators of resource subsidies (the cross-boundary movement of energy, nutrients, or materials). This topic may have theoretical and empirical implications because non-native species may play a major role in ecosystem connectivity by transporting—or interrupting the transport of—energy and organic matter. Therefore, the main aims of this review were to (1) assess temporal trends, geographic distribution, and methodological approaches in research on resource subsidies mediated by non-native species; (2) synthesize how non-native species alter the magnitude, direction, and dynamics of resource subsidies across ecosystems and their implications for ecosystem functioning; and (3) identify key gaps in current knowledge and define future research priorities.
